rows.title: terminal: notify terminal emulator about test session progress

outcomes.text: The new `TerminalProgressPlugin` uses `Literal` and `Session` in type annotations but these names are not imported. Add `from typing import Literal` and import `Session` from the appropriate pytest module.
`write_raw` is now a public method but the class does not expose it in its `__all__` or documentation. Consider adding a short docstring to clarify its purpose and that it bypasses markup handling.

The plugin is registered whenever `reporter.isatty()` is true, but the feature can be disabled via `-p no:terminalprogress`. Registration should respect the plugin manager's built‑in disabling mechanism (i.e., only register if the plugin name is not already disabled).

rows.title: [truncate explanation] Fix edge case when we truncate due to max_chars

outcomes.text: When max_lines==0 the code falls through to the branch that adds an ellipsis unconditionally. This means that even if no lines were actually truncated (e.g. when max_chars==0 and the input fits), the output will still end with "...", which is misleading. Consider guarding the ellipsis addition with a check that something was actually truncated.

The calculation of truncated_line_count uses int(need_to_truncate_char) to account for a partially truncated line, but this does not handle the case where max_lines==0 and no lines were removed. The count may be off by one in that scenario.

rows.title: Fix: assertrepr_compare respects dict insertion order

outcomes.text: The order of keys in the `obtained` dict has been changed from the original order (passed, skipped, failed) to (failed, passed, skipped). While the dict comparison is order‑agnostic, keeping a stable order can aid debugging and consistency with other parts of the code. Consider restoring the original key order or documenting the intentional change.

`_pprint_dict` now iterates over `object.items()` directly, preserving insertion order. This is intentional for the bug fix, but note that callers relying on sorted output will need to be updated accordingly.

`repr_dict` now uses `islice(x, self.maxdict)` to respect insertion order while truncating. Ensure that `self.maxdict` is set appropriately in tests; otherwise the truncation may not reflect the intended behaviour.
The test `test_saferepr_dict_preserves_insertion_order` verifies that the new `repr_dict` preserves insertion order. If future changes modify the iteration order, this test will catch regressions.
The new test `test_dict_extra_items_preserve_insertion_order` checks that assertion diffs display dict keys in insertion order. This aligns with the change in `SafeRepr` and `pprint`.

`repr_dict` now returns a string with the same formatting as the original `reprlib.Repr.repr_dict`. Verify that the formatting (e.g., spaces after commas) remains consistent with the rest of the pretty‑printer output.
